title: Permission validation suite: canonical scenarios, audit-replay tests, and SAML admin flows
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: RBAC v2 introduces a richer permission model (resource-scoped roles, conditional grants, and admin-only operations exposed via SAML SSO). We need a robust validation suite that exercises canonical permission scenarios, replays audit logs to detect regressions, and verifies SAML admin flows end-to-end.

Goal: Create an automated, CI-executable suite that serves as the authoritative source of truth for permissions behavior across Hosted/Dedicated/Private runtimes. The suite should catch regressions introduced by kernel scheduling, routing changes, or auth middleware refactors.

Scope:
- Canonical scenario definitions covering: owner/admin/editor/viewer scopes, cross-tenant isolation, delegated admin, and conditional grants (time-bounded/scoped).
- Audit-replay tests: ingest recent anonymized audit slices and verify that permission outcomes match expected decisions.
- SAML admin flows: full OIDC/SAML login + admin role mapping, group sync sim, and edge-case SAML assertions (missing NameID, multiple attributes).
- CI integration: run in PRs for core auth changes and nightly full-run on main.
- Artifacts: compact fixture pack (JSON lines) + human-readable scenario matrix.

Approach and decisions:
1) Canonical scenarios: define ~60 scenarios as rows in a CSV-style matrix (action, resource, principal, expected allow/deny, required audit fields). This reduces brittle per-endpoint tests. We will store canonical scenarios in /data/rbac/canonical_scenarios.csv in the repo.
2) Deterministic mocks vs production replay: for unit PR fast checks, use deterministic mocks of policy engine. For regression detection, use the audit-replay runner against a sanitized audit slice pulled from the audit-archive S3. Trade-off: replay increases flakiness from env differences; mitigate via containerized runner and pinned DB snapshot.
3) SAML test harness: leverage a lightweight SAML IdP container (samltest-sh style) in CI and create mapper configurations that replicate customer IdP attribute mappings. Also include negative cases (expired assertion, missing group attribute).
4) Failure modes and tolerance: tests that validate non-security behavior (e.g., telemetry fields) will be flaky and run only in nightly; blocking PRs will only run the core permission matrix and SAML happy path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Core permission matrix (60 scenarios) passes in PR-stage CI job named ci/rbac/permission-matrix on main branch.
- Audit-replay runner executed nightly with results uploaded to the security dashboard at /dashboards/rbac/regressions.
- SAML admin flows validated in integration test job ci/rbac/saml-integration with IdP container.
- New test artifacts and scenario CSV checked into repo; minimal docs in Confluence (link below).

Deliverables:
- test/canonic_matrix_runner.py (runner for matrix)
- test/saml_harness/ (IdP config & scenarios)
- ci/jobs/permission-matrix.yaml and ci/jobs/saml-integration.yaml
- docs/confluence/RBAC-v2-permission-validation (procedure + runbook)

Risks and mitigation:
- Flaky audit replay: mitigate by snapshotting the DB and running replay in isolated container with pinned dependencies.
- Secret handling for SAML test IdP: use ephemeral test certs stored in vault with restricted access.
- Performance: running full matrix against live runtime can be slow; we will parallelize scenarios and restrict detailed nightly runs to a single canary region.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Define the CSV schema and add initial 60 scenarios (owner: Gabriel).
- Implement PR CI job for permission-matrix (owner: Aisha).
- Wire nightly audit-replay pipeline into security dashboard (owner: SRE).

Notes on observability: failures should attach the policy decision trace ID and the relevant audit event IDs. The runner will produce a minimal failure report with the scenario row, request payload, policy decision log excerpt, and link to the raw audit event.
